name: Passkey MFA to Home
summary: A password-proved user with a pending MFA challenge completes a valid user-verified Passkey assertion for the challenge-bound account, consumes the MFA challenge, and receives the authenticated application session.

preconditions.expression: session-capability == anonymous and a password-issued MFA challenge is active for an existing durable identity and provider passkey is included in the challenge's allowed providers

serverInteraction.intent: Validate the password-issued MFA challenge for provider passkey, use its UserId to issue and validate a user-bound Passkey assertion requiring user verification, advance the signature counter, consume the MFA challenge only after successful Passkey proof, and establish the platform-appropriate application session.

postconditions.expression: credential-proof == passkey-proved, the password-issued MFA challenge is consumed, and session-capability in [authenticated-limited,authenticated-normal]

sourceReferences.note: The same canonical Passkey continuation surface is reused for primary Passkey and password-bound Passkey MFA; the active MFA challenge determines which server orchestration is used.

The MFA begin/complete/token endpoints validate provider=passkey, derive UserId from the password-issued challenge, delegate cryptographic proof to the existing user-bound Passkey manager, and consume the MFA challenge only after successful proof.
Challenge validation enforces allowed-provider and durable-user binding; challenge consumption is single-use.
The existing user-bound Passkey primitive validates WebAuthn challenge ownership, credential ownership, user verification and signature counter advancement.
When both TOTP and Passkey are enabled, either allowed provider may satisfy the same password-issued MFA challenge; devices unable to perform Passkey may complete with TOTP instead.
